source_text: Klagel. Jerem. 1, 22. Ἐπιφυλλίσαι δὲ τὸ μετὰ τρυγητὸν τὰ βραχέα τῶν καταλειφθέντων ἐπιτρυγᾶν, ὃπερ ποιοῦσιν οἱ πένητες. ὥσπερ οὖν ὃτε μὲν ἐπεσκόπεις ἐπιμελῶς, ἐκάθαιρες τὰ κλήματά μου, πάντα τὰ χείρονα μέχρι τῶν σμικροτάτων περιαιρῶν >τῆς σταφυλῆς τῆς καὶ τοῦ βότρυος τῆς πικρίας<, οὕτω τοὺς ἐμοὺς ἐχθροὺς τοῦτο γάρ μοι λυσιτελές, εἴγε μετ' αὐτοὺς τελείως σωθέντας κἀγὼ κατὰ τὴν σήν, ὦ κύριε, κρίσιν τεύξομαι σωτηρίας· οὒς ὁρὼσα λελύπημαί τε σφόδρα καὶ κατέγνων ἐμαυτῆς, τῆς ἐπισκοπῆς τῆς παρὰ σοῦ δεομένη.
pass_a_gloss: And “to glean” is after vintage to gather the small things of what was left, which the poor do. Just as, then, when you were overseeing carefully, you were cleansing my branches, taking away all the worse things even unto the smallest—of the grape and of the cluster of bitterness—so do this to my enemies; for this profits me, if after they have been completely saved I too according to your judgment, O Lord, will obtain salvation; whom seeing I have both been greatly pained and condemned myself, needing the episkopē / oversight from you.
pass_b_english: And “to glean” (Lamentations 1:22) is after vintage to gather the small things of what was left, which the poor do. Just as, then, when you were overseeing carefully, you were cleansing my branches, taking away all the worse things even unto the smallest—of the grape and of the cluster of bitterness—so do this to my enemies; for this profits me, if after they have been completely saved I too according to your judgment, O Lord, will obtain salvation; whom seeing I have both been greatly pained and condemned myself, needing the oversight from you (Deuteronomy 32:32).

choices.why: Origen’s Lam 1:22 turns on punitive-yet-healing divine visitation.

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Origen’s Greek Lamentations fragments. Sense checked against Klostermann GCS III. Modern English not copied. OET = no previous English translation.
